title: Sensex ends over 870 points down, Nifty50 below 22,900 - top reasons for fall

title: Asian Para Games: Kokila stuns world champion en route to judo silver
content: Kokila from India has elevated her previous bronze medal achievement to a silver at the Asian Para Games held in Aichi-Nagoya. She showcased her skill by narrowly defeating reigning world champion Yi Liu in the semifinals. Although she faced Aibike Ulanbek Kyzy in the final, who clinched gold with a swift ippon, Kokila's silver illustrates her increasing prowess in the -52kg para-judo category.

title: Paid to do nothing for a year: Google AI rule that UK PM Andy Burnham wants gone
content: The UK plans to legislate against non-compete clauses, PM Andy Burnham announced in Manchester, calling them a drag on innovation. The move hits Google DeepMind, where some London staff were reportedly barred from joining rivals for up to a year, often on paid garden leave. It comes as DeepMind researchers, including Nobel laureate John Jumper and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer, leave for Anthropic and OpenAI.

title: Svitolina announces split from Monfils: ‘Marriage is ending, but our family is not’
content: Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils have decided to part ways after a tough year, focusing on their commitment to their daughter Skai. Svitolina shared that her emotional challenges significantly influenced their separation. Both athletes are asking for understanding and privacy during this transition as Monfils also announced plans to retire from professional tennis.

title: Girl gifted to Queen Victoria at 7; great-great-grandson revisits her life
content: In 1850, a seven-year-old African girl named Aina was presented to Queen Victoria as a diplomatic 'gift' after losing her family and spending two years in captivity. Renamed Sarah Forbes Bonetta, she grew up under royal protection but faced restrictions on her freedom. Now, 176 years later, a new biography is examining her life, while her great-great-grandson, Bayo Randle, reflects on her struggles, achievements and complicated relationship with the British monarchy.

title: Elon Musk to Dario Amodei: I do not agree with your donation of Anthropic shares
content: Anthropic has announced a pledge of 5% of its shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, with the possibility of donating an additional 2% for every 50% valuation increase from a baseline. Co-founders and team members have committed roughly 20% of their equity. This fund will focus on public benefit initiatives and may also support traditional nonprofits. Further information about its governance and structure is anticipated soon.

title: Indian paintings of Alexander sold for £70,760, over 88 times estimate
content: Recently, six exquisite paintings portraying moments from Alexander the Great's life captivated bidders at an auction. Originating from North India around 1500, these pieces were initially valued between £600 and £800, yet they soared to an astonishing £70,760 at Lyon & Turnbull. Their connection to the Persian literary heritage and the Sultanate era underlines the remarkable blend of art and storytelling within our rich cultural history.

title: ‘Product which failed every time’: Shivraj mocks Rahul for 'expiry date' remark
content: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan responded to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's prediction about the BJP's decline. Chouhan called Gandhi's remarks laughable, labeling him a failed product. Gandhi addressed a public gathering in Goa, urging voters to support Congress in the upcoming elections. He accused BJP leaders of corruption and electoral malpractice during his speech at the Congress’s ‘Goy Rakhon Yatra’ event.

title: Army officer's car broke down after repairs; commission orders free repair, Rs 50k
content: A consumer commission in Delhi found Youwe and Cars guilty of inadequate service after repairs. The commission mandated the service centre to repair the vehicle at no charge and provide compensation. An Army officer's Nissan car developed issues shortly after repairs from waterlogging damage. The commission also noted the service centre's failure to explain costs properly after multiple estimates.

title: London woman loses 48cm boundary fight over neighbour’s kitchen extension
content: In a surprising turn of events, a homeowner in Surbiton, London, lost a legal dispute concerning a narrow 48-centimetre strip of land. It was determined that the neighbours' kitchen extension had effectively claimed squatters' rights, having occupied the land uncontested for over two decades. The First-tier Tribunal's decision highlights crucial insights into property borders and emphasizes the importance of diligent title plan checks for prospective buyers to avoid future complications.

title: Asian Para Games: Kapil Parmar bounces back from semifinal defeat to win bronze
content: Kapil Parmar achieved a remarkable feat by winning a bronze medal in the men’s J1 -70kg judo competition at the Asian Para Games. His victory came when he defeated Indonesia's Rafli Ahnaf Shidqi by ippon in an impressive match lasting just over a minute. In another notable achievement, Kokila, a visually impaired athlete, reached the finals after defeating Yi Liu of China.

title: Tiger Shroff firing case: A minor, bike taxi driver - what we know about shooters
content: Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the shooting at actor Tiger Shroff's car. The arrests took place at Kota railway station while they were traveling from Mumbai to Delhi. The actor was leaving a football club when assailants opened fire on his vehicle. Eyewitness accounts describe how the attackers fled on a motorcycle after the shooting.

title: Indian-origin couple’s $100,000 dream cafe damaged in Australia arson attack
content: Ashish Sharma and Manali Purohit's dream of running their vegan cafe 'And Bodega' in Fitzroy North, Melbourne, turned tragic when it suffered extensive damage from an arson attack shortly after opening. This incident, linked to a nearby tobacco shop, cost them their life savings and brought additional theft. To recover, they initiated a crowdfunding campaign and are searching for new locations, buoyed by the unwavering support of their community.

title: Kodak ran uranium-based research device for 31 years beneath Rochester lab
content: For 31 years, Kodak operated a uranium-based research device beneath its Rochester laboratory, using it to examine materials and detect impurities. Installed in 1975 and shut down in 2006, the machine attracted public attention in 2012 because it contained highly enriched uranium. A new Popular Mechanics report explains how the device produced neutrons through nuclear fission but could not sustain a chain reaction independently, making it different from a conventional nuclear reactor.

title: Maharashtra woman who earned Rs 200 in fields now manages 12-acre family farm
content: In Pachod village, Sunita Nehare transformed her family's agricultural methods, dramatically boosting crop yields. Despite early challenges with disappointing harvests, she secured management rights of the family land. By integrating advanced farming practices, she not only amplified cotton production but also embraced crop diversification for a sustainable future. With an annual income of around ₹2.

title: Ludhiana school horror: Peon gropes, kisses teen student, records video
content: A school peon in Ludhiana has been arrested for allegedly molesting a 16-year-old student. The victim's mother filed a complaint after her daughter described the incident that occurred in the teacher's office. According to the complaint, the peon physically assaulted the girl while she searched for a book. Additionally, the mother claimed the peon recorded a video of the assault without consent.

title: 'Geography is real': Rubio says India-US trade deal close, explains stance on Russian oil
content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that negotiations on a trade deal with India are close to finalization. He emphasized the importance of India's energy needs before implementing sanctions on Russian oil imports. Rubio highlighted that energy diversification is challenging for countries like India despite their efforts. Additionally, he mentioned ongoing global pressures on energy supplies that complicate these situations.

title: Salman Ali Agha joins elite list featuring Dhoni, Yuvraj Singh with record ODI feat
content: Salman Ali Agha delivered an impressive performance by scoring 107 runs from 90 balls against Sri Lanka, marking a significant milestone in the tri-series. This victory saw him break Mohammad Yousuf's record as the most prolific No. 5 centurion for Pakistan. The match concluded with Pakistan triumphed by 37 runs, following a collapse from the Sri Lankan chase, highlighting Agha's essential contribution to the team's strength in the middle order.

title: BJP veteran LK Advani discharged from Delhi hospital after health improves
content: BJP veteran and former deputy prime minister LK Advani, 98, was discharged from Delhi’s Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Monday after his health improved. The BJP stalwart Advani was admitted on October 16 with a chest infection and remained under medical observation, including a stay in the intensive care unit (ICU).

title: Gen Z officer Jaya Sharma's journey from DSP to IPS through UPSC
content: Jaya Sharma’s journey from Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) in Haryana to the Indian Police Service (IPS) highlights her determination to achieve her career goals. A mathematics graduate from Delhi University and postgraduate from IIT Delhi, she also worked on a research project at ISRO before entering policing. Despite demanding job responsibilities, she continued preparing for the UPSC Civil Services Examination. After her selection for the IPS, she was allotted the Andhra Pradesh cadre and posted as ASP in Adoni.

title: G.O.A.T! An Se-young ends Susi Susanti’s 29-year reign with record 47th title
content: An Se-young has made history by surpassing Susi Susanti's impressive record of 46 titles, clinching her 47th international title with a thrilling win against Akane Yamaguchi in the Denmark Open final. This remarkable achievement contributes to her reign as world No. 1 for 105 weeks and highlights her extraordinary prowess in women's singles badminton, even overcoming an ankle injury during the match.

title: Michigan to ban uncertified untreated firewood from 2027 to block 140+ pests
content: Michigan will ban untreated, uncertified firewood from entering the state starting January 1, 2027, to prevent the spread of more than 140 plant pests and diseases. The restriction will apply to travellers, campers and businesses, with exemptions for certified, heat-treated wood and certain other wood products. Authorities will focus on public awareness in 2027, while repeat violations could attract fines of $1,000 to $10,000 from 2028.

title: Gaza potter builds clay shelter for parents after family loses home
content: In the face of displacement from war, Jaafar Atallah crafted an innovative dome-shaped home from local clay for his family. Along with his community, he explored the potential of mud bricks, resulting in sturdier shelters compared to standard tents. This method emerges amidst Gaza's pressing housing crisis, driven by material shortages. Neighbors are also embracing recycled resources, ensuring traditional expertise evolves to tackle the region's housing emergency.

title: Kerala’s ‘suicide tree’ linked to hundreds of deaths and forensic mystery
content: Othalanga, or the suicide tree, flourishes along Kerala's shores, but its perilous fruit contains cerberin, a lethal toxin that can disrupt heart rhythms, leading to potentially fatal outcomes. Between 1989 and 1999, numerous deaths were connected to othalanga poisoning, posing diagnostic challenges for medical professionals due to symptom overlap. Raising awareness about this dangerous plant is crucial for prevention and timely treatment.

title: Highly intelligent women may face harsher judgment at work than men: Study
content: Studies reveal that women with high skills frequently face mistreatment and difficulties in workplace relationships, a challenge less common for men. While male colleagues often receive backing, women are scrutinized through the lens of gender stereotypes. Such biased views can affect women's effectiveness in team settings. It is imperative for organizations to objectively assess abilities, free from gender biases that may influence the support received.

title: Who is Mona Agarwal? Paralympics medallist sets Asian Para Games record to win gold

title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Oppn targets Fadnavis govt with 'jungle raj' claims
content: the opposition on Sunday targeted the Maharashtra government over the firing incident involving the actor . he alleges that the incident reflected a deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state . the opposition leaders cited previous attacks and killings while questioning the government’s handling of public safety .

title: Katy Perry's arts camp has reached nearly 1,000 kids; permanent site planned
content: camp firework is an arts-focused summer programme created by Katy Perry and her sister angela Lerche to give underserved children a space to explore, connect and discover their potential . nearly 1,000 middle school students attended 12 camps over seven years, state a recent report by KEYT News Channel .

title: Zelenskyy flags warning gap before Russian strikes; Rubio denies intel pause
content: the overnight strikes across 11 Ukrainian regions damaged more than 10 energy facilities and left at least 5,50,000 households without electricity . the comments come as US secretary of state Marco Rubio denies that the US had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine .

title: Australian woman lawmaker critically injured in vehicle attack; driver arrested
content: the 65-year-old was hit by a car outside her district office in Wangaratta . she was airlifted to hospital with critical injuries . her family confirmed her identity in a statement . police initially withheld the victim's name in accordance with privacy protocols .

title: Watch: Russian satellite chases Ukraine-linked spacecraft in space; raises alarm
content: Russia's Kosmos 2612 has adjusted its orbit to match that of ICEYE-X36 . a commercial radar-imaging satellite linked to Ukraine's military has manoeuvred into close proximity with the satellite . it raises concerns that Moscow could be monitoring or potentially interfering with Western space assets .

title: Oregon teen who rescued elderly couple from crash receives lifesaving medal
content: 16-year-old Elijah Buckwald helped rescue an elderly couple . he climbed onto an overturned pickup truck and opened the door . at 14, he helped strangers trapped inside after a serious crash . the instinct to step forward has earned the Redmond teenager national recognition .

title: Watching videos on speaker in trains? You could face a fine, even jail
content: a nuisance in Metro rail also attracts a penalty and such persons can be removed from coaches . the move could bring relief to railway passengers disturbed by people playing music or watching videos on their phones . people persisting with such an act could even face up to six months of jail and up to Rs 5,000 penalty .

title: UN agency WFP to cut food aid to Gaza as funding crisis threatens millions
content: families in hard-to-reach areas, including those near the Yellow Line marking the area of military control, will receive meals every other day instead of daily . the number of people receiving flour bags and food ration boxes will also fall from 1.1 million to 600,000 each month . cash assistance for half a million people had already been cut since July .

title: 'Protocol, not power': Ex-IMF director punctures Pakistan's 'historic milestone' claim
content: former IMF executive director Krishnamurthy Subramanian challenged the claim that the role is a return to global financial leadership . he said the chairmanship was ceremonial and rotated annually, arguing that it should not be equated with leadership of global economic forum .

title: ‘We will all die one day’: Ecuador priest killed by falling crucifix
content: patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari died at the church of Perpetual Relief in Guayaquil . he was facing the congregation and appeared not to notice the crucifix falling behind him . livestream captured worshippers rushing to help as cries for assistance were heard .

title: Manipur violence: Protesters place bodies outside CM's bungalow after militant attack
content: two people were killed by suspected militants near the border of imphal and Kangpokpi districts . police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters . four others were also injured after suspected militant opened fire on firewood collectors .

title: 'Holiday mode on': BJP alleges Rahul travelling abroad to meet 'chaos collaborators'
content: the BJP claimed that Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader Rahul Gandhi has left for another foreign vacation . he asked if he was travelling to meet his 'chaos collaborators' a man who spends more time chilling than working-and then shouts, 'Vote Chori!'
